Action Plan:
1. Empiric treatment for suspected simple urinary tract infection: prescribe either Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days; advise generous oral hydration and consider cranberry juice.
2. Safety-netting: patient to call or re-attend if no improvement by the end of the week or sooner if fever, flank/back pain, or systemic symptoms develop (possible pyelonephritis).
3. Sexual activity advice: avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception thereafter.
4. Pregnancy considerations: advised to perform a pregnancy test if any doubt about pregnancy status.
5. Document antibiotic allergy (Clindamycin) in chart to guide prescribing.
6. Offer first sexually transmitted infection (STI) screen at convenient time.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 3-day history of burning/stinging on micturition and mild lower abdominal “cramping” pain.  
• Hematuria: small amount noted once today.  
• Urine odor: malodorous.  
• No urinary frequency, urgency, flank pain, nausea, vomiting, or fever.  
• Bowels normal; no diarrhea.  
• Gyn/sexual history: sexually active with 1 partner (boyfriend, 2 months); condoms used; last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago”; never had an STI screen; does not believe she is pregnant.  
• Past medical history: irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• Medications: none regular; tried over-the-counter sodium bicarbonate (dose/route/frequency not documented) without relief.  
• Allergies: Clindamycin → swelling (likely angioedema).  
• Social: 19-year-old college biology student; lives with friends; non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially on weekends.

Objective:
• Telehealth visit; no vitals or physical examination documented.  
• No laboratory or imaging investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria / Suspected simple cystitis  
   - Assessment: Likely uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection.  
   - Investigations planned: None at this encounter (no urinalysis or culture ordered).  
   - Treatment planned: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim 1 tab PO BID × 3 days; increase fluids; consider cranberry juice.  
   - Safety-net: Return/call if worsening, fever, flank pain, or no improvement by week’s end.

2. Pregnancy possibility  
   - Assessment: Unlikely but not excluded.  
   - Investigations planned: Home or clinic urine pregnancy test if any uncertainty.  
   - Treatment planned: N/A.

3. Sexual health counselling  
   - Assessment: Sexually active without prior STI screen.  
   - Investigations planned: Offer full STI screen at convenient time.  
   - Treatment planned: Temporarily abstain from intercourse until UTI symptoms resolve; continue condom use.  
   - Relevant referrals: Sexual health clinic if preferred.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: vitals, abdominal/renal physical exam, urinalysis and culture, medication dosing specifics (exact drug chosen, mg strength), STI screen not performed, pregnancy test not done.  
● Internal conflicts: LMP reported by patient as “a couple of weeks ago,” yet doctor documented “three weeks ago” – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor audio dropouts but clinically adequate.
